MARKET.head: Langtons' first Global Live Auction sells over $400,000, its largest ever
MARKET.summ: Australian fine wine authority Langtons has unveiled the results of its inaugural Global Live Auction, which has gone down as its largest to date in its 38-year history. The Global Live Auction featured a line-up of first classified wines from both the Langtons Classification of Australian Wine and the newly launched...
takeaways: Langtons' inaugural Global Live Auction, held 6 November at the Art Gallery of NSW, raised over $400,000 against a $277,000 valuation.
A 2010 Domaine de la Romanee-Conti magnum was the top lot at $112,125, and Krug and Dom Perignon lots sold well above estimate.
Henschke Hill of Grace ($14,950) and Bass Phillip Reserve Pinot Noir ($5,750) set Australian auction records, with clearance above 80%.

MARKET.head: Billy Button Wines wins two trophies and 25 medals at Mildura show
MARKET.summ: Alpine Valleys winery Billy Button Wines enjoyed a successful weekend in early November at the 2026 Australian Alternative Varieties Wine Show (AAVWS) in Mildura, taking home two prestigious trophy awards and an impressive 25 medals. The winery competed against a field of 700 wine entries at the AAVWS, with the show featuring...
takeaways: Billy Button Wines won two trophies and 25 medals at the 2026 Australian Alternative Varieties Wine Show in Mildura.
The winery took the Helen Healy Award for Excellence, given to the top exhibitor across multiple wine classes.
Its Vermentino won the Provenance Award, judged across the 2016, 2023 and 2025 vintages together.

MARKET.head: Adelaide study says global wine crisis is structural, not cyclical
MARKET.summ: While boom and bust cycles have characterised national wine industries for decades, new Adelaide University research illustrates that the current global wine crisis is “different from previous downturns and far more concerning”. Adelaide University said that the research draws on “decades of annual data on both non-premium and...
takeaways: Adelaide University research led by Professor Kym Anderson finds the current global wine crisis differs from past downturns and is more severe.
Global wine consumption has fallen by a quarter since the 1960s, while beer and spirits volumes have doubled.
Between 2013 and 2022, premium wine sales grew 3.1% a year while non-premium sales fell 2.2% annually.

MARKET.head: Australian wine stocks fall to lowest since 2019-20 as production drops 18%
MARKET.summ: The Australian wine industry produced less wine than it sold, helping reduce excess stock in 2025-26, according to Wine Australia’s latest Production, Sales and Inventory Report. The 2025-26 findings “indicate the sector has made progress in reducing stocks, but further adjustment is likely to be needed to move to a more...
takeaways: Wine Australia's 2025-26 report shows national wine inventory fell 9% to 1.87 billion litres, the lowest since 2019-20.
Total wine production fell 18% to 925 million litres, while sales dropped 4% to 1.04 billion litres.
Wine Australia expects winegrape prices to stay below long-term averages through vintage 2027.

MARKET.head: French wine imports to China jump in September on restocking and cheaper 2024 Bordeaux
MARKET.summ: China’s imports of French wine surged in September 2026, with their value rising nearly 130% from August and volume almost doubling
takeaways: China imported 4.44 million litres of French wine worth US$73.69 million in September 2026, per Vino Joy News customs data.
Value rose 129.70% and volume 96.61% from August, with France overtaking Australia as the largest source by value.
Importers cite year-end restocking and lower 2024 Bordeaux en primeur prices, with Lafite cutting about 29% from 2023.

MARKET.head: Changyu partners with South Korea's Ayoung as China profits fall 19%
MARKET.summ: With profits down nearly 20% despite rising sales, Changyu has struck a deal with South Korean drinks group Ayoung to put its wines in supermarkets, specialist shops and restaurants and hired a local team to build demand beyond the first shipment
takeaways: Changyu, China's largest wine producer, signed a South Korean distribution deal with importer and retailer Ayoung Group.
Changyu's first nine months of 2026 revenue rose 6.51% to RMB 2.254 billion, but net profit fell 19.25%.
South Korea's first-half 2026 wine imports fell 3.18% in volume to 27.07 million kilograms, while value rose 1.71%.

MARKET.head: SWR completes benchmark of 40-plus global wine sustainability standards
MARKET.summ: (5 min read) Over the past three years, SWR has embarked on the mammoth process of benchmarking the more than 40 sustainability standards that exist globally in wine. Mammoth because the documentation of a standard can easily surpass 1500 pages of documents. The rationale for this when we started was simple.
takeaways: SWR has benchmarked more than 40 global wine sustainability standards over three years, with a few small ones still to evaluate.
Its Global Reference Framework scores standards across 39 topics, and the OIV is using it to revise its definition of wine sustainability.
Packaging and logistics is the most widespread gap, with few standards setting more than cursory requirements there.

MARKET.head: Fungus-resistant grape varieties cut Apulian table grape protection costs 55%
MARKET.summ: Towards Sustainable Viticulture: Cost Savings and Reduced Chemical Use through Fungus-Resistant Grapevine Varieties
takeaways: Galati et al. (2026) found adopting fungus-resistant grapevine varieties in Apulian table grape production cut plant protection costs by 55%.
The same study found extended gross margins rose 7%-8% without reducing gross revenues, and cost variability fell.
The study was published in Wine Economics and Policy.

MARKET.head: Regenerative Sonoma vineyards match conventional farm returns over 30 years
MARKET.summ: Economic viability of regenerative viticulture in Sonoma County, California IVES Technical Review adapted from Herrera et al. 2026
takeaways: A 30-year cost-benefit study compared regenerative and conventional management across four Sonoma County vineyards, published by Herrera et al. in 2026.
Regenerative vineyards returned financial results close to conventional farming when grape yields were maintained, with site fit and operational strategy deciding success.
Regenerative vineyards had lower establishment costs but higher annual operating costs from compost and sheep grazing, while labor dominated expenses in both systems.

MARKET.head: Pridham urges grower-led regional collaboration to build a resilient Australian wine industry
MARKET.summ: In the third instalment of his series examining the future of the Australian wine industry, Ben Pridham from Prodham Viticulture in McLaren Vale moves beyond the problems to consider what comes next. Drawing on his own business experience and examples from overseas, he makes the case for regional collaboration, grower-led...
takeaways: Ben Pridham of Pridham Viticulture in McLaren Vale, the third in a series, argues for regional collaboration and grower-led decisions in Australian wine.
He cites Argentina, where Mendoza's grower-inclusive approach produced about 61% of national wine and over 90% of exports, versus under 7% for San Juan.
He points to South Australia's $109 million Wine Industry Transition and Growth Package, including a $100 million loan scheme to move unviable vineyards to other uses.

MARKET.head: Bordeaux holds 41% of traded wine value as Burgundy's share climbs
MARKET.summ: Bordeaux claimed 35.7% of traded value. Burgundy and Champagne followed closely behind
takeaways: Bordeaux claimed 41% of the week's traded value on Liv-ex, the wine trading exchange, strengthening its lead.
Burgundy's share rose from 15.7% to 20.8%, with Domaine de la Romanee-Conti and Domaine Leflaive leading by value.
Champagne's share fell from 13.0% to 8.5%, while Tuscany claimed 11.6% led by Soldera and Sassicaia.

MARKET.head: Top Burgundy wines grow scarce in China as allocations tighten
MARKET.summ: Some of Burgundy’s most sought-after wines are becoming harder to source in China, importers told Vino Joy News, as smaller harvests and tighter allocations constrain supply
takeaways: Importers in China say supplies of DRC, Leroy, Leflaive and Domaine Gros Frère et Sœur tightened from July this year.
Fine West CEO Wu Xianghua says Leflaive's entry-level whites sold out after the estate cut allocations to China.
Shanghai Boyun's Lin Jianbing says prices for leading Burgundy wines fell considerably over the past two years, so demand does not explain shortages.

MARKET.head: English sparkling wine expands fast, but overproduction is crashing grape prices
MARKET.summ: After a decade of rapid growth and rising international recognition, English sparkling wine faces the challenge of turning enthusiasm into sustained sales
takeaways: English sparkling wine plantings rose 510 percent from 2005 to 2024, reaching 4,841 hectares, per Wines of Great Britain.
Overproduction has pushed English grape prices down about 50 percent after the large 2023 harvest, reaching historic lows by end of 2025.
English wine exports grew 35 percent from 2023 to 2024, with the US a leading market for producers such as Gusbourne.

MARKET.head: AWRI re-elects two board directors and appoints Steven Weinert as director
MARKET.summ: The Australian Wine Research Institute (AWRI) has announced the re-election of Corrina Wright and Brett McClen to its board as well as the appointment of Steven Weinert as a director. Voted by wine grapes levy payers, Corrina Wright was re-elected in the ‘small wine grapes levy payer’ category (up to 2,000 tonnes) and Brett...
takeaways: The AWRI re-elected Corrina Wright and Brett McClen as directors, with new terms starting 1 January 2027.
Steven Weinert was appointed director from 1 November 2026 and will chair the board audit committee.
Trish Giannini and Sarah Courtney left the board on 31 October 2026, after Courtney's Liberal Party Senate preselection.

CULTURE.head: VinePair lists 30 wines for Thanksgiving 2026, favoring low-alcohol, high-acid bottles
CULTURE.summ: Amid the marathon of planning, prepping, cooking, and baking, finding the perfect wine for Thanksgiving isn’t always the top priority. If wine is on the checklist, venturing into bottle shops this time of year can be especially dizzying and sometimes even stressful. So many choices, so little time to choose, and what’s my budget?
takeaways: VinePair's tasting staff picked 30 Thanksgiving wines from bottles reviewed across its buying guides this year.
Selection favors high acidity, lower alcohol and flavours that suit the holiday meal, including American wines like New York Merlot.
Recommended varieties include Riesling, Cabernet Franc, Pinot Noir, Gamay and Chenin Blanc, with off-dry styles for sweeter dishes.

SCIENCE.head: Grapevine leaf tissue sampling: when and what to test for nutrients
SCIENCE.summ: WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 25, 2026. BY STAN GRANT, VITICULTURIST. This is the third and final article in a series on laboratory analysis as a component of vineyard mineral nutrient management.
takeaways: Vineyard nutrient analysis uses grapevine tissues sampled at set growth stages, with bloom the traditional collection time.
Veraison sampling gives wineries early warning of nitrogen needs before fermentation, plus time to correct ripening nutrients.
Petioles are customarily sampled in California and the New World, while leaf blades are preferred elsewhere.

SCIENCE.head: Biochar in vineyard soils: review weighs productivity and carbon sequestration
SCIENCE.summ: The use of biochar in agricultural soils: Impacts on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration
takeaways: Leonel J.R. Nunes's review, published November 2026 in Science of The Total Environment, examines biochar use in agricultural soils.
The paper assesses effects on vineyard productivity and the potential for carbon capture and sequestration in vineyard soils.

SCIENCE.head: Review assesses tools for keeping dry-farmed vineyards resilient under water stress
SCIENCE.summ: The study provides a narrative and critical literature review evaluating the physiological, agronomic, and practical tools available to enhance vineyard resilience under dry-farming conditions, and analyzes grapevine strategies for managing water stress. Published by Poni et al 2026 in Agronomy, MDPI Headline Findings Results
takeaways: Poni et al. (2026) in Agronomy review physiological and agronomic tools for dry-farmed vineyard resilience.
The review analyses grapevine strategies for managing water stress under rainfed conditions.
Related studies cover biochar, nitrogen-fixing biostimulants, and fungus-resistant grape varieties for sustainable viticulture.

SCIENCE.head: Winter cover crops plus foliar biostimulant matched tilled Syrah yields in Spain
SCIENCE.summ: Pairing winter-spring cover crops with a foliar nitrogen-fixing microbial biostimulant supports sustainable rainfed viticulture through complementary soil and plant pathways, boosting soil nutrient enzymes while keeping yields and juice traits competitive or improved
takeaways: A 2020-2021 rainfed organic Syrah trial in southern Spain compared year-round tillage with winter-spring cover crops.
Cover crops raised soil nutrient enzyme activity and decomposition potential, while high-dose Methylobacterium biostimulant matched or beat tilled yields.
Combining cover crops with the high biostimulant dose also showed possible synergy in juice °Brix and pH, per the study, published March 2027.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Rogovila - Wine is Culture
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Celebrating Slovenian garagiste David Bratož, plus the family's new releases
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: David Bratož, founder of Rogovila in the Vipava Valley, Slovenia, died in November 2025 after falling ill with leukaemia.
Rogovila produces around 4,000 bottles a year from half a hectare of old vines, with uncertified organic farming and minimal additives.
After David's death, his daughter Lana, who has a full-time office job, continues the winery with help from her mother and two sisters.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Gonzalo Guzmán, a talented winemaker producing interesting wines across Chile, and an advocate of Mencia and Albariño
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I caught up with Gonzalo Guzmán over dinner at La Bistrot Lastarria in Santiago, to taste through some
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Gonzalo Guzmán left El Principal in Pirque in 2020 after 16 harvests as its winemaker to focus on his own project.
Guzmán makes his wines at Ojdfjell, where he rents part of the winery, and has planted vines in Itata.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Inside This Year’s Hospices de Beaune Auction: The Drama, the Records and the Wines That Found Their Buyers
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Discover the drama and record-breaking moments from this iconic Burgundy charity wine auction, featuring exceptional barrels and the buyers who claimed them
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jonathan Finch
takeaways: The 166th Hospices de Beaune auction raised €14.4 million at the hammer, down from €18.8 million last year, with 348 red and 86 white barrels offered.
Average white Burgundy barrel price fell to €39,893 from €58,580, while red rose 5 per cent to €28,931.
The Clos de Vougeot Grand Cru charity barrel sold for €770,000 to Alaor Pereira Lino of Anima Vinum, and the Faiveley family's extra €230,000 brought the charity total to €1 million.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Wine News: What I’m Reading the Week of 11/22/26
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Hello and welcome to my weekly roundup of the wine stories that I find of interest on the web. I
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: Beaujolais Anew
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The 2026 release of that wine we love to hate and hate to love, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: In the 1970s, Georges Duboeuf and other négociants began marketing Beaujolais Nouveau beyond France, with the slogan "Le Beaujolais Nouveau est arrivé!".
Marcel Lapierre, Jean Foillard, Guy Breton and Pierre-Marie Chermette helped pioneer natural winemaking in Beaujolais, producing Nouveau by low-intervention methods.
Randall Grahm's documentary The Terroirist covers his plan to plant vines grown from seed on a San Juan Bautista property; Grahm is 73 and has Parkinson's.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Cabernet Franc in the Press: November 2026
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Livermore wins Region of the Year, Wine Spectator profiles Loire Cabernet Franc, Decanter takes a cross-border look at Ontario and New York, and much more
NEWSLETTERS.author: Cab Franc Chronicles
takeaways: Wine Enthusiast's 2026 American Wine Region of the Year award went to California's Livermore Valley.
Livermore Valley is known for Sauvignon Blanc and Cabernet Franc, which its regional association named its signature white and red varieties in February 2025.

NEWSLETTERS.head: More Than Skin Deep: A Grape with a Colourful Past
NEWSLETTERS.summ: A colourful tale of the grape that was born to dye and the father-son team behind it
NEWSLETTERS.author: Eveline Chartier
takeaways: Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier, Champagne's black grapes, have colourless juice, so Blanc de Noirs Champagnes are white wines made from black grapes.
Garnacha Tintorera, also called Alicante Bouschet, is a teinturier grape with red flesh, bred in 19th-century France by Louis and Henri Bouschet.
Henry Jeffreys reported that a top Burgundy producer reportedly grows Alicante Bouschet to boost the colour of his Pinot Noir, though it is not authorized in Bourgogne wine.

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Many Sins Of Wine Critics
NEWSLETTERS.summ: In the exciting (other adjectives are available) times we’re living in, we’re often told that writing is passé, people just don’t bother reading words anymore. A few journalistic outlets, especially in the financial press, seem to have finally come clean about the seriousness of their reporting, by auto-summarising their pieces...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: Tim Atkin argues wine critics are judged on expertise, with the US favouring tasting ability and Britain favouring knowledge and scholarship.
Atkin says critics should be slightly more expert than their target audience, and that conflicts of interest extend beyond payment to dining, politics and friendships.
He criticises the 30-second tasting ritual, comparing judging wine that way to reviewing a movie from its trailer.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Find Rare Shizz With Orpheus Alerts!
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Some (more!) exciting news, folks: As many of you already know, sometimes wines get featured on here that are pretty rare. I’m talking about the kind of stuff that either doesn’t make it to the big platforms, or, if it does, is either priced astronomically or is gone in milliseconds. Understandably, that can be somewhat […]...
NEWSLETTERS.author: Joe Roberts
takeaways: 1WineDude is partnering with Orpheus Alerts, part of Orpheus Intelligence Labs Inc., to help buyers find rare wines.
Orpheus monitors sources like local-language catalogues, merchant inventories, auction notices, and restaurant or estate sales.
Users create alerts using natural-language descriptions and can upload images; Orpheus notifies them when a matching wine is available and connects them with the seller.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Roadshow Review: Spain Brings Value Wines to China
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Does any nation offer better wine value than Spain? This seems obvious to French bottlers, who import major amounts of Spanish wine each year. Per
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jim Boyce
takeaways: Spain ranked fifth by volume in China last year, narrowly behind Italy and a quarter of leader Australia, per WBO stats.
Spain dropped to sixth by value in China, below New Zealand, with per-liter value above only Chile among the top eight sources.
The Wines From Castilla, La Mancha Roadshow stopped in Beijing and will be in Guangzhou on November 6, with value-priced wines like DCOOP's Airén and Tempranillo.
